title: How Much Information Can We Fit inside a Transformer?
abstract: arXiv:2610.34553v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How efficiently can transformers store factual knowledge? The answer to this question has implications for both model design and understanding the limits of transformer-based systems. Prior studies observe a linear relationship between the number of facts memorized and the number of model parameters required, substantially worse than what theoretical analyses predict is achievable. We re-examine empirical scaling: through rigorous and systematic experiments, including extensive hyperparameter search via Bayesian optimization, we determine the smallest model that can perfectly memorize a given set of facts, and measure how this minimum size scales with the number of facts. translated_abstract: Transformer能够以多高的效率存储事实性知识？这个问题的答案对于模型设计以及理解基于Transformer系统的能力极限都具有重要意义。此前的研究观察到，模型记忆的事实数量与所需参数数量之间呈线性关系，这远差于理论分析所预测的可达到水平。我们重新审视了这一实证缩放规律：通过严谨而系统的实验，包括利用贝叶斯优化进行的大规模超参数搜索，我们确定了能够完美记忆给定事实集合的最小模型，并测量了这一最小模型规模如何随事实数量的增长而缩放。在由随机抽取、彼此独立且无可利用结构的（主语，关系，宾语）三元组构成的合成数据集上（例如（Paris, capital_of, France）），我们发现记忆容量——即模型能够完全记忆的最大数据集规模……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过贝叶斯优化超参数搜索等严谨系统性实验，确定了能完美记忆给定事实集合的最小Transformer模型规模，并重新测量了事实记忆容量随模型规模的缩放规律。
en_tdlr: This paper rigorously re-examines how transformer memorization capacity scales with model size, determining the smallest model that can perfectly memorize given sets of random factual triples through extensive Bayesian-optimized hyperparameter search.
